gen-dafont-nulshock-gf-marcellus-sc: Technical and stretched out, Nulshock traces every letter in one unshaded outline. Marcellus SC takes over below with gentle stroke modulation and dignified, pulled-back terminals, so the heading feels engineered while the text feels literary.
gen-dafont-nulshock-gf-montagu-slab: Montagu Slab brings a traditional text serif with sturdy downstrokes and slender turns beneath the wide-set Nulshock. Its restrained thick-and-thin gap is the pair's best trick.
gen-dafont-nulshock-gf-noto-serif-hentai: Nulshock stretches its spacious, swell-free outlines wide, like letters drawn with a single technical pen. Noto Serif Hentaigana follows with a text serif whose weight shifts gradually; give it a modest size.
gen-dafont-nulshock-gf-ovo: Ovo reads classic and sure of itself, with shallow ascenders under a tall middle band. Over a longer stretch its thins barely lighter than its thicks keep the eye moving without any snap, a quiet foil to Nulshock's hairline-free strokes.
gen-dafont-origami-gf-domine: Brushy, blunt and unmistakable. Origami draws every stroke at one weight, while Domine below adds modest modulation and a breathing space inside each curve, which lets a long page of text move along comfortably.
gen-dafont-origami-gf-esteban: Origami's flat, unmodulated brush strokes sit like poured lead type, heavy and singular. Esteban follows as a text serif whose strokes taper only slightly, so a long passage glides along with its wide-open e never pinched.
gen-dafont-origami-gf-faustina: Faustina reads classic and authoritative, its bowls thinning gently rather than sharply. Origami's tubing-bent letters beside it feel like a bold hand-painted sign next to a well-made book, each making the other's restraint or swagger clearer.
gen-dafont-origami-gf-halant: Hand-painted and chunky, with no hairlines to vanish. Origami's brush strokes meet Halant, a serif with a faint but real thick-thin shift and outward-pointing terminals, and the two sit together like a sign above a stately shopfront.
gen-dafont-origami-gf-headland-one: Origami's one-gauge brush strokes make the single most distinctive mark, like a sign painter's line never lifted. Headland One settles beneath as a classic serif with gentle weight variation, its well-spaced letters giving the heavy heading room to stand.
gen-dafont-origami-gf-hedvig-letters-ser: Origami paints its letters at constant width, with bowls as heavy as stems, which makes it a loud and memorable heading. But Hedvig Letters Serif is the one built for sustained text, with open curves and sturdy lowercase to carry the page.
